next_steps: Read the most relevant passages in full with get_text(ref, context=2) before relying on them.
If the passages found are off-target, call again with key_terms in Greek or Latin (e.g. "ἀγάπη", "gratia"); accents are optional.
Use get_work_info on a work to see its versions: for the New Testament the Greek SBLGNT is the original, the Vulgate and the English Bible are translations.
Before answering, pass every citation and quote you will use to verify_citations.

tool_descriptions.research_question: START HERE for any question. Finds passages in the New Testament and the church fathers for a question in plain language, by meaning and by key_terms, and returns them grouped by period (New Testament and Apostolic Fathers, Apologists, Nicene and Post-Nicene, ...), earliest first, with short excerpts and next steps. key_terms: 2-4 Greek or Latin words a scholar would search for (e.g. ["δικαιοσύνη", "iustitia"]); accents are optional. Excerpts are leads: read passages in full with get_text before relying on them.
tool_descriptions.get_text: Exact text of a passage or range: New Testament as book chapter:verse ("John 1:1-5", "1 Cor 13:4", "Rom. 3:21"), fathers in their standard citation ("1 Clement 5.1", "Eusebius, Church History 3.39.15"), or words of one segment ("John 1:1@1-3"). context=N adds N segments before and after. Returns the original (Greek for the New Testament) and the translations per segment (Latin Vulgate, English), with the version used for each line, a fingerprint of the exact text and the build id.
